{{Short description|Kra language spoken in China}} {{Infobox language |name=A'ou |states=China |region=[[Guizhou]] |speakers=50 |date=2011 |ref=e25 |familycolor=Tai–Kadai |fam2=[[Kra languages|Kra]] |fam3=Ge–Chi |fam4=[[Gelao languages|Gelao]] |script= |iso3=aou |glotto=aoua1234 |glottorefname=A'ou }} '''A'ou''' (阿欧方言) or '''Red Gelao''' (红仡佬语) is an endangered [[Gelao languages|Gelao]] language spoken by fewer than 100 people in [[Guizhou]], [[China]].Li Jinfang [李锦芳]. 2006. ''Studies on endangered languages in the Southwest China'' [西南地区濒危语言调查研究]. Beijing: Minzu University [中央民族大学出版社]. Only the Hongfeng (红丰) and Bigong (比贡) [[dialect]]s are still spoken, each with only a few dozen speakers. ==Dialects== The main dialects of A'ou, which all have limited [[mutual intelligibility]], are: *Hongfeng (红丰)Zhou Guoyan 周国炎. 2004. ''Gelao zu mu yu sheng tai yan jiu 仡佬族母語生态硏究 (Studies on the linguistic ecology of the Gelao people)''. Beijing: Ethnic Publishing House 民族出版社. *Bigong (比贡)Li Xia; Li Jinfang; Luo Yongxian. 2014. ''[https://web.archive.org/web/20150402110929/http://www.peterlang.com/index.cfm?event=cmp.ccc.seitenstruktur.detailseiten&seitentyp=produkt&pk=78134 A Grammar of Zoulei, Southwest China]''. Bern: Peter Lang AG, Internationaler Verlag der Wissenschaften. {{ISBN|978-3-0343-1344-5}} *Qiaoshang (桥上)Ostapirat, Weera. 2000. "[http://sealang.net/sala/archives/pdf8/weera2000proto.pdf Proto-Kra]." ''Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area'' '''23''' (1): 1-251. (extinct) Only one elderly speaker of the Houzitian (猴子田) dialect was found in 2013, and it is likely now extinct.Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. ''[https://zenodo.org/record/1122531 Red Gelao (Houzitian) audio word list]''. {{doi|10.5281/zenodo.1122531}} [[Mulao language (Kra)|Mulao]] (木佬) is sometimes also included, in addition to [[:zh:羿语|Yi]] (羿), an extinct A'ou [[Variety (linguistics)|variety]] of [[Sichuan]].Zhang Jimin 张済民. 1993. ''Gelao yu yan jiu 仡佬语研究 (A study of Gelao)''.
